lines.t: In the middle of a top secret meeting, a British commander pulled out a pistol... and shot a block of ice.
Because the navy had a problem. Steel. Every warship needed thousands of tons of it, and there wasn't enough.
So an inventor had a crazy idea. Build an aircraft carrier... out of ice.
Not a small one. Two thousand feet long. Two million tons.
So they mixed the water with wood pulp, like wet sawdust, and froze it.
You see, normal ice is like glass. One crack runs straight through. But wood fibers work like hair in a braid. The crack hits a fiber... and gets stuck.
They built a little test ship on a lake in Canada. When they switched off its cooling motor, it took three hot summers to melt.
At a big meeting with the top generals, they wheeled in two blocks. Plain ice, and the new stuff.
A general swung a chopper. The plain ice split in two. The new block barely dented, and his arms rattled.
Then the commander pulled his pistol. Bang! The plain ice shattered.
Bang! The second bullet hit the new block... and bounced right back out...
and grazed the trouser leg of an American admiral.
But the giant ice ship was cancelled. The reason?
Would you sail on a ship made of ice? A, yes. Or B, absolutely not.
